\author{}
\date{2026-04-29}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty: medium.}  The issue is not a missing analytic
  estimate, but a mismatch between the size hypothesis printed in the paper and
  the size hypothesis consumed by the present pasting route.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} about \textbf{3--6 scalar or boundary
  lemmas} if one proves a smaller-\(k\) saturation argument, or a theorem-level
  correction if the present large-\(k\) route is retained.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \textbf{10\% Mathlib} and
  \textbf{90\% project-local}.  The arithmetic is elementary; the substance is
  deciding which LDT theorem statement is justified by the paper's pasting
  pipeline.
  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} elementary order arithmetic on natural
  numbers and nonnegative real error parameters.  The main inputs are the
  project-local statements of the main induction, pasting, and final scalar
  cascade.  Tracked in \ghissue{906}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key theorem forms}

The comparison involves three theorem forms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Printed source form.}  The theorem in
  \path{references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex} assumes \(k\ge md\), and its
  successor proof assumes \(k\ge (m+1)d\).
  \item \textbf{Pasting-input form.}  The pasting theorem used in the successor
  proof requires \(k\ge 400md\) in the restricted \(m\)-dimensional slice.
  \item \textbf{Current formal-interface form.}  The Lean theorem
  \leanid{MIPStarRE.LDT.MainInductionStep.mainInduction} and the final theorem
  \leanid{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal} use the corrected large-\(k\)
  interface, displayed in the blueprint as separate current-interface entries.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The assertion}

This note concerns the \(k\)-hypothesis in the main induction theorem of
\cite[Section~\emph{The main induction step}]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}, and
its use in the proof of the main formal soundness theorem.
\footnote{The original discrepancy was recorded in \ghissue{906} and first
implemented in \ghpr{912}.  The documentation issue for this note is
\ghissue{928}.  In the TeX source consulted here, the main induction theorem is in
\path{references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex}, lines 7--18; the successor step
is in the same file, lines 429--568; and the pasting theorem used there is in
lines 299--330.}
Here \(m\) is the number of variables, \(q\) is the field size, \(d\) is the
individual degree bound, and \(k\) is the sampling parameter in the consistency
estimates.  The integer \(k\) is carried unchanged through the induction on
\(m\).

In the theorem as stated, an \((\varepsilon,\delta,\gamma)\)-good symmetric
strategy for the \((m,q,d)\) low individual degree test is assumed to satisfy
only
\begin{equation*}
  k\ge md.
  \tag{\path{thm:main-induction}}
\end{equation*}
Under this hypothesis, the theorem produces a polynomial measurement
\(G\in\operatorname{PolyMeas}(m,q,d)\) satisfying the advertised consistency
estimate.  The same \(k\)-condition is then inherited by the stated main formal
soundness theorem after the reduction from a general two-prover strategy to a
symmetric one.

\section{The use of pasting}

The successor step proves the induction theorem in dimension \(m+1\) assuming
the theorem in dimension \(m\).  In that step the ambient strategy is a strategy
for the \((m+1,q,d)\) test, and the proof assumes
\begin{equation*}
  k\ge (m+1)d.
  \tag{\path{sec:proof-of-main-induction}}
\end{equation*}
This is sufficient to apply the induction hypothesis to each \(x\)-restricted
strategy, since the restricted strategies have dimension \(m\), and
\((m+1)d\ge md\).

After the restricted measurements have been improved to projective
submeasurements, the proof pastes them into a measurement in dimension \(m+1\).
The pasting theorem invoked at this point has its own size hypothesis.  In the
notation of the successor step, it requires
\begin{equation*}
  k\ge 400md.
  \tag{\path{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section}}
\end{equation*}
This condition is not a consequence of \(k\ge (m+1)d\).  For instance, when
\(m=1\) and \(d>0\), the latter allows \(k=2d\), whereas the pasting theorem
requires \(k\ge 400d\).  Thus the argument as written does not justify the
successor step throughout the interval in which \(k\ge (m+1)d\) but
\(k<400md\).

Equivalently, the missing implication is
\[
  k\ge (m+1)d
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  k\ge 400md,
\]
which is false for the relevant range of parameters.  The issue is therefore a
missing side condition, not a notational convention or a peculiarity of the
formal language.

\section{The corrected formal interface}

The repair made in the checked formal statements is to state explicitly the
hypothesis used by the proof.  The source-labelled blueprint theorem is now
stated with the corrected bound \(k\ge 400md\).  In the successor step from
\(m\) to \(m+1\), one assumes \(k\ge 400(m+1)d\).  This immediately supplies the
pasting hypothesis \(k\ge 400md\) needed for the restricted dimension.

\title{The Zero-Sampling Boundary in the Main Formal Theorem}
\author{}
\date{2026-05-22}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty: low as a mathematical obstruction, medium as a
  formal repair.}  The scalar obstruction is immediate from the factor \(k^2\)
  in the printed final error; deciding the replacement theorem form requires a
  source-statement judgment.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} no new proof machinery is expected if the
  formal theorem is corrected to require \(k>0\).  A fully formal
  counterexample would require a small explicit projective strategy with
  nonconstant point answers in degree zero.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \textbf{5\% Mathlib} and
  \textbf{95\% project-local}.  The only arithmetic is the simplification of the
  displayed error at \(k=0\); the issue concerns the LDT theorem statement.
  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} elementary arithmetic on nonnegative real
  error parameters.  The project-local inputs are the zero-\(k\) simplification
  of the final error and the degree-zero evaluation fact for polynomial-valued
  measurements.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let \(\sigma\) be the projective strategy in the low individual degree test.
Write \(m\) for the number of variables, \(q\) for the field size, \(d\) for
the individual degree bound, \(k\) for the sampling parameter, and \(\eps\) for
the test-passing error, so that the strategy is assumed to pass the test with
probability at least \(1-\eps\).  The final consistency error in the source
theorem is denoted by \(\nu\).  With this notation there are three relevant
theorem forms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Printed source form.}  The theorem
  \path{thm:main-formal} assumes \(k\ge md\) and gives the three final
  consistency conclusions at
  \[
    \nu =
    100000 k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/40000}+(d/q)^{1/40000}
      + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\right).
  \]
  \item \textbf{Current checked nonzero form.}  The present formal route proves
  the corrected two-space source theorem under \(k\ge 400md\) and \(0<k\).  The
  role-register construction and the subsequent scalar absorption are checked
  inside the theorem, not supplied as external hypotheses.
  \item \textbf{Zero-sampling boundary.}  If \(d=0\) and \(k=0\), the printed
  hypothesis \(k\ge md\) is satisfied, but the displayed error is exactly
  \(0\).  The theorem then demands exact consistency with degree-zero
  polynomial measurements.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The source assertion}

The source theorem in \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} states the final
soundness theorem for an integer \(k\ge md\).%
\footnote{Tracked in \ghissue{422}.  The relevant source passage is
\path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}, lines~180--202.}
This condition admits the boundary case \(k=0\) exactly when \(d=0\).  At that
boundary the printed error parameter is
\[
  100000\cdot 0^2\cdot m^4
  \left(\eps^{1/40000}+(0/q)^{1/40000}
    + e^{-0/(2560000m^2)}\right)=0.
\]
Thus the conclusion is no longer an approximate consistency statement.  It is
an exact consistency statement.

This is stronger than what the test-passing hypothesis implies.  If
\(\eps\) is allowed to be large, the hypothesis that the strategy passes with
probability at least \(1-\eps\) imposes no exact agreement condition on the
point measurements.  In degree zero, however, every polynomial outcome is a
constant function on \(\F_q^m\), so a polynomial-valued measurement evaluates to
the same answer-valued measurement at every point.  A strategy whose point
measurement gives different deterministic answers at two different points can
therefore satisfy the printed hypotheses for a sufficiently large \(\eps\), but
cannot be exactly consistent with a single degree-zero polynomial measurement

\section{Key theorem forms}

The paper's printed line-169 replacement would preserve the error

bound
\[

The checked local repair uses the pre-completion orthonormalization estimate
and the monotonicity of canonical completion to obtain the sharper corrected
bound
\[

  \simeq_{\zeta_1+10\zeta_1^{1/8}}
  I \otimes G^{\mathrm B}_g.
\]
This bound is the one recorded by the projectivization-chain repair lemmas.

\section{The cited step}

This note concerns the projectivization step in the proof of the main induction
theorem in \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.\footnote{Tracked in
\ghissue{1099}. In the TeX source consulted here, the relevant passage is in
\path{references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex}, lines~150--180, and the
specific replacement step is lines~167--173.}
At this point in the argument, the paper has already produced polynomial-outcome
measurements $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ with consistency error
$\zeta_1$, projective submeasurements $P^{\mathrm A}$ and
$P^{\mathrm B}$ from orthonormalization, and completed projective measurements
$Q^{\mathrm A}$ and $Q^{\mathrm B}$.

The paper first states the pre-projective consistency estimate

\section{Key theorem forms}

The source asks for an error function
$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)$ satisfying
\[
  \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)
    = \operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)
\]
and bounding the final consistency defect whenever the three input defects are
at most $\delta$ and the codeword-collision probability is at most $\eta$.
Under the paper's global convention, the displayed polynomial assertion means
that there is a universal $C>0$ such that
\[
  \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta) \leq C(\eta\delta)^C
  \qquad (\eta,\delta>0).
  \tag{product contract}
\]
The imported proof instead accumulates terms depending separately on the two
errors, including $O(\delta^{1/2})$, $O((\delta+\eta)^{1/2})$, and $\eta$.
A compatible corrected theorem form would use, for example, an upper bound by
$A(\eta^r+\delta^s)$ for universal $A\geq1$ and $r,s>0$.
The polynomial shorthand itself is only an upper bound on positive inputs;
it supplies neither axis values nor an additional nonnegativity condition.
The corrected predicate supplies both on the closed nonnegative quadrant.

\section{The source assertion}

Lemma~\texttt{lem:pasting} of \cite[lines~504--525]{Ji2020MIPStar} imports
Fact~4.35 from the NEEXP paper.  Its error is declared to be
$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$.  The asymptotic convention in
\cite[lines~19--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} requires every variable to occur in the
product on the right side of the product contract.  The proof of the imported
fact, however, bounds the two sources of error independently; see
\cite[lines~1030--1209]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.%

\subsubsection{Bit string representations}
\label{sec:ff-representations}

As mentioned at the end of \Cref{sec:tms}, we sometimes treat the
inputs and outputs of Turing machines as representing elements of a finite
field, or a vector space over a finite field.
We discuss some important details about bit representations of finite field
elements and arithmetic over finite fields.

In the paper we only consider fields $\F_{2^k}$ where $k$ is odd. 

\begin{definition}\label{def:admissible-size}
  A field size $q$ is called an \emph{admissible} field size if $q=2^k$ for odd
  $k$.
\end{definition}

Elements of $\F_2$ are naturally represented using bits. 
To represent elements of $\F_{2^k}$ as binary strings we require the
noncomputable section

/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter tuple.  Its scalar carrier
uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
is blueprint
`def:admissible`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
structure AdmissibleParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- Every admissible parameter tuple has positive ambient dimension. This
follows from positivity of the admissible field size and the divisibility
`P.m ∣ P.q` in `def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
  have hqpos : 0 < P.q := by
    rcases P.hq with ⟨k, _, hq⟩
    rw [hq]
    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)
  exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr
    (ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hqpos) P.hdvd)

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
This is blueprint `def:admissible-size`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
-/
def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k

/-- An admissible field size is at least two, its binary exponent being odd
and therefore positive.  This is a property of blueprint
`def:admissible-size`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
-/
theorem IsAdmissibleSize.two_le {q : ℕ} (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) : 2 ≤ q := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hqk⟩ := hq
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hk
  rw [hqk, hj]
  calc 2 = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 * j + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)

The final name check found one incorrect ledger FQN: `twisted_commutator_avg_le_explicit` is in `MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting`, not directly in `MIPStarRE.QPBT`. Its file, line, and bound are correct.

The review will request report corrections for the native-error notation, the mixed-tail formula, the stale proof description, and that FQN. The implemented headline formulas and the checked comparison certificates otherwise agree with the inspected source.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `docs/error-bounds.md:646` — **Mathematical: the native error uses an undefined/reused `Q`.** Earlier, line 488 defines `Q` as the fixed coefficient. The native construction instead requires \(Q=Q_0e^{1/8}\), and line 805 also needs the missing definition \(L_{\mathrm{ext}}=mH_0(e^{1/256}+r^{1/16})\). These are the quantities used by [ExplicitConstants.lean](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-730-error-bounds-report/MIPStarRE/QPBT/ExplicitConstants.lean:35) and [QuantitativeScalars/Bounds.lean](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-730-error-bounds-report/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/QuantitativeScalars/Bounds.lean:51). With the report’s existing constant interpretation, \(64Q>1\) forces \(G=1\) even at zero error, contradicting the later fractional estimate in sufficiently small regimes. Distinguish the coefficients from their error functions explicitly, as the ledger already does.

- [ ] F2 (changes) `docs/error-bounds.md:731` — **Mathematical formula error, apparently typographical:** the mixed low-degree tail must be \(2^{-\tau hd}\), not \(2^{-\tau Md}\). Here \(h=2m+2\), whereas `M` denotes the later fractional dimension factor. Paper `lem:ld-soundness`, `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:414`, and [deltaLd](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-730-error-bounds-report/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameMeasurements.lean:377) put the actual test dimension in this exponent. The displayed expression therefore does not retain the claimed exact tail.

- [ ] F3 (changes) `docs/error-bounds.md:853` — **Editorial: the proof description is stale.** Lines 868–898 describe a degree-two construction branching on \(I_{\mathrm{raw}}<4\). The final [degree-two theorem](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-730-error-bounds-report/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QuantitativeSoundness.lean:368) instead takes the fractional theorem’s witness and applies \(H\le I\). Preserve the calculation as a historical or alternative derivation, but describe the actual final proof accurately. Likewise, line 594 names the existential `exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one`; the native rounded construction actually calls `direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one_any_strategy_at_native_error` at `Combining/ExtendedLineGame/RoundedPolynomialEstimates.lean:338`.

- [ ] F4 (changes) `docs/bound-ledger-qpbt.md:169` — **Editorial: incorrect declaration reference.** The FQN is `MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.twisted_commutator_avg_le_explicit`, as confirmed by `Observables/ExpandedCommutation.lean:188` and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:2088`. The ledger omits `ProjectiveSetting`. Also correct `docs/error-bounds.md:1834`: its `pauli-soundness` link selects lines 40–64, containing the explicit baseline; `pauli_soundness` begins at line 110.

Reviewed the clean, docs-only head `03a7536c2240b925af2d6cebefd5b5dd3566f2ca`. These findings concern the new documents; they do not reopen PR #736’s unchanged proofs.

|---|---|

Constants, separate parameter powers, three simultaneous conclusions, and strictness qualification agree. The report correctly retains \(k\ge400md,\ k>0\) and discloses the wider printed domain. |
| QPBT baseline and headlines | Checked the symbolic explicit baseline, exponent gain \(625/8\), fractional dimension powers, clipping/capping, field/qubit statements, and common witness. The headline \(H\) agrees with Lean. |
| Native and separated estimates | Checked \(\Lambda_h\), rounding, ordered/mass estimates, six-term \(U_s/L_s\), \(B_G\), separate extraction certificates, and mixed state/raw-operator bounds. Subject to F1, the displayed formulas match. The unrestricted construction and restricted scalar estimates are correctly distinguished. |
| Fractional constants | Confirmed \(664\cdot16218+368=10769120\) and \(3\cdot304^2=277248\). The global-pair estimate needs no ratio upper bound. The coefficient 14596 is correctly identified as unimplemented. |
| Candidate inventory | Confirmed all 16 LDT and 31 QPBT entries, including their gain, impact, cost/risk, and disposition. The report distinguishes improvements to the source argument from recovered formalization losses and keeps #735 unimplemented. |
| Comparisons | Independently checked the capped \(F\le I\le C\) and \(H\le I\le C\) arguments, strictness conditions, and both \(L=121,128\) incomparability families. No ordering against native mixed components is improperly inferred. |
